_readme: The closed responsibility register from battle-engine-ssot.md section 3, made mechanical.
The register is the owner's eleven plus eight additions accepted 2026-09-16. It skips #13,
which was retracted the same day: five IIntentSource implementations are five policies plugged
into one seam, not five copies of a mechanism, and calling that a defect was the expensive
direction to be wrong in. The numbering keeps the gap so the retraction stays visible.
A 'decision' is the arithmetic or branch that IS the mechanism, never the name of it. Calling
the owner's function is reuse and passes; writing the owner's formula out again is a second
owner and fails, whatever the local variables are called. That distinction is the whole point:
guard-class-system.ps1 used to be a positive-presence check a hand-copied reflect formula would
pass; combat-math-dedup T4 (2026-09-23) added a negative half over the analytic and siege files,
A mechanism with no decision pattern carries a note saying why, because a row that says nothing
looks exactly like a row that is enforced. A note is not an exemption - it is an admission,
and every one of them names what would close it.
Every allow entry names the module that removes it. An exception with no owning module is how

decisions.what: Subtracting a defense magnitude from a power magnitude — the mitigation decision itself, not a call to the primitive that performs it

allow.why: D7 — subtractive defense against a shipped divisive default, with no base-damage term and no amp or crit, while its own comment claims it is identical to the resolver

decisions.what: Building a crit multiplier as one-plus-a-contest — the crit damage decision. Both spellings match on purpose: the owner now reaches the curve through ElementalResolver.Contest, and a second owner writing CombatProbability.Sigmoid inline is the same decision made twice

allow.why: X5 — the analytic estimator re-derives the resolver's crit shape instead of being pinned to it
X5 — the same re-derivation in the sim tool. G2's own finding was that no guard scans tools/ at all

decisions.what: Deciding a contest between two actors by putting their difference through the logistic curve. Calling ElementalResolver.Contest is reuse and passes; calling CombatProbability.Sigmoid directly is deciding the contest yourself

allow.why: The function itself. A declaration is not a second decision, and excluding it by pattern would also exclude the owner
X5 — the analytic estimator decides its own hit/crit contests instead of calling the resolver
X5 — the same three contests again in the sim tool

Found 2026-09-17 by registering this pattern: siege decides its own hit chance rather than resolving through the engine's elemental sub-module, so a siege swing reads omni-only accuracy while every other mode reads omni + element. Rule 4 — a mechanism one mode has differently
Found the same way: the delve's difficulty seam decides a dodge contest of its own against BattleRuleset.BaseDodge. Same finding as siege, different mode

decisions.what: The logistic curve written out — every contest in the engine goes through this one declaration

mechanisms.name: Shield
mechanisms.note: Conforming today by the 2026-09-16 audit: DamageApplyPipeline reaches ShieldGate on both the battle and lawn apply paths. Absorption order is a branch rather than a formula, so no text pattern separates the decision from a call to it. `battle-effect-math` revisits this when it wires the battle bag's CombatMath.

mechanisms.name: Targeting and area effect
mechanisms.note: Conforming today: the dispatcher, EffectBag, StatusEffectBridge, StatusSpread and ActionTargetResolver all call TargetResolver.Resolve. Area shapes are a closed vocabulary guarded elsewhere, and a second owner would be a second shape enum rather than a copied formula.
mechanisms.waits-on: no module — recorded as conforming, re-checked by the close audit

mechanisms.name: Resource resolve and consume
mechanisms.note: Conforming today, and deliberately so: BattleRunState.cs:129 uses LawnActorResourcePools verbatim with a comment saying it avoided a near-duplicate type. This is the law applied correctly before it was written down.
mechanisms.waits-on: no module — recorded as conforming, re-checked by the close audit

mechanisms.name: Proc and trigger condition (atom runtime scope)
mechanisms.note: The trigger vocabulary is 13 strings with one declaration since 2026-09-16 and is already guarded. The defect here is D3 — 9 of the 13 never fire in battle — which is an absence, not a second owner, so this guard cannot see it. `battle-effect-math` owns closing it.

mechanisms.name: Action system
mechanisms.note: No decision pattern yet. Cost, cooldown and envelope are ledger operations rather than formulas, so a second owner appears as a second ledger type — which `guard-actor-hub.py`'s shape would catch better than a text pattern would. Named here so the gap is visible.

mechanisms.name: Injury and permanent death
mechanisms.note: D10 — permanent death is delve-local. ExtractionSettlement decides Retire/Recover/Roster for a delve and no other mode has an equivalent, so today's owner is a mode rather than the engine. `death-and-injury` promotes it, and writes this row's pattern.

mechanisms.name: Equipment damage in battle
mechanisms.note: No implementation anywhere — every 'durability' hit in source is an unrelated word-sense. Owner ruling 2026-09-16: owned by the `species-gear-chain` program, not this one, and struck from the remediation fix list. It stays a registered responsibility with a named owner rather than disappearing.

mechanisms.name: All battle derived stats and their mechanisms
mechanisms.note: Already enforced, by a guard of the right shape: scripts/guard-actor-hub.py refuses a second composer. Duplicating that here would give the same rule two owners, which is the defect this register exists to refuse.

mechanisms.name: The unified virtual clock — initiative, turn order and scheduling
mechanisms.note: D15 — the lawn runs two time bases at once: status timing reads the injector's wall clock while DoT scheduling reads the kernel's 100 ms event queue. That is one board with two notions of when, which is a second owner this guard cannot see, because the second owner is a wiring choice rather than a copied formula.

mechanisms.name: Movement and board position
mechanisms.note: Battle-only today (A9/A10 TryMoveTowardNearestEnemy, siege board). Under section 3c the engine owns whether a move is legal and what it costs; where to move is AI. No pattern separates the two yet.

mechanisms.name: Death, cleanup and body state
mechanisms.note: Different per mode today — ImmortalCharges and entity grant withdrawal do not agree across modes. Distinct from permanent death (#9): this is the corpse and the cleanup, not the roster verdict.

mechanisms.name: Summon / spawn during battle
mechanisms.note: One atom kind (`spawn.entity`) against a closed 18-kind registry that is already guarded. A second owner would be a nineteenth kind, which that guard refuses.
mechanisms.waits-on: no module — enforced by the atom-kind registry guard

mechanisms.name: Kill attribution
mechanisms.note: D9 — absent outside the lawn, and on the lawn the general horde has no owner row, so no empire earns from it. An absence, which this guard cannot see; recorded so the register does not read as conforming.

decisions.what: Deciding what a reflect contest is between — which channels are read, and for whom. The dispatcher owns this because it is the only place that knows the incoming hit's element payload

Dividing a reflect delta by a reflect scale inline. This is the D8 formula itself, and after T2.3 it has exactly one owner — ElementalResolver.RateFromZero — which takes the scale as an argument and so does not spell the channel name. A file that still names ReflectRateScale or ReflectShareScale as a divisor is writing the formula out again

allow.why: The third copy, found by this guard on 2026-09-17. The two Core copies are gone: the dispatcher and PhaseModel both call ElementalResolver.RateFromZero now. This one is the POC reference the port is measured against, so extracting it changes what 'reference' means — T2.7's stated default is to leave it pinned by estimator-parity rather than delete it

mechanisms.name: Determinism and seeded RNG streams
mechanisms.note: Not a feature but a property: a mode whose randomness is not seeded per stream cannot be replayed. Seeded streams exist in battle only, which is an absence elsewhere rather than a second owner here.

mechanisms.name: Victory / defeat and settlement
mechanisms.note: Per mode today — the delve settles through ExtractionSettlement and the other modes each differ. Shares an owner file with #9 because the delve decided both in one place; separating them is part of what `death-and-injury` does.
